title: The Deep Safehouse
premise: August Zhou, a burned-out financial-crimes investigator, is handed a ledger by a stranger who claims August once saved his life — a favor August has no memory of. The ledger exposes a laundering network run through three governments' own intelligence slush funds, and the stranger is murdered within hours of delivering it. Hunted by an assassin contracted to bury the paper trail and discredited by his own agency, August must smuggle the truth across a contested border checkpoint before the night shift rotates and his window closes forever. He gets the ledger out at terrible cost — exposing the network but losing his old identity, his name, and any chance of ever sleeping as himself again.
about_author: Gideon Reyes spent eleven years auditing offshore accounts for a firm he no longer names, before trading spreadsheets for sentences. He writes thrillers from a coastal town where, he insists, the money is clean.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: August Zhou, sleepless and hollowed out by an incident he can't name, is cornered in a parking garage by a sweating stranger named Ilya who insists August saved his life in Riga two years ago. August remembers nothing. Ilya leaves him a flash drive and a warning: 'They'll come for the interest.' POV: August. Beat: dread disguised as ordinary life cracking open.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: August decrypts the drive at his office: ledgers tracing billions through intelligence slush funds in three countries, all laundered into legitimate markets — including accounts he personally certified as clean. His own signature is on the paperwork. POV: August. Beat: vertigo; the investigator realizes he may be evidence.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: August returns to find Ilya dead in his hotel room, staged as a heart attack, and a professional already waiting for him — a woman with a customs badge and a silenced pistol he barely escapes. He grabs the backup copy Ilya hid and runs. POV: August. Beat: terror; the abstract threat becomes physical.

chapters.title: The Woman from Customs
chapters.summary: The assassin, Mara Voss, reports to her handler that the ledger survived; she's ordered to recover it 'quietly' because three governments would rather it vanish than burn. We learn she keeps meticulous records of every kill — her own private justice. POV: Mara. Beat: cold competence hiding a conscience.

chapters.title: Ghost Signature
chapters.summary: August reaches his old mentor, Elena Marsh, now retired, who confirms the Riga operation was real — and that August was there, his memory chemically suppressed after he witnessed something. The favor happened. He just wasn't allowed to remember it. POV: August. Beat: identity fracture; the past rewrites itself.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: Elena helps August map the network: officials in all three governments are clients, meaning no embassy, no police, no court is safe. Their only route is a journalist at a border-town radio station who can broadcast the ledger before anyone can suppress it. POV: alternating August/Elena. Beat: grim clarity — the law itself is compromised.

chapters.title: Checkpoint
chapters.summary: August travels toward the border under a forged identity while Mara closes in, using his own investigative patterns against him. At a fuel stop he recognizes her surveillance and deliberately feeds her a false route. POV: split August/Mara. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension; hunter and hunted mirror each other.

chapters.title: The Night Shift
chapters.summary: Mara corners August at the checkpoint hours before the shift change will seal the crossing. Instead of killing him, she demands to read the ledger — and finds her handler's name among the payees. She has been laundering the very money she was paid in. POV: Mara. Beat: betrayal; her private code collapses.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Together, improbably, they fight through the checkpoint during the chaotic shift change — Mara turning her skills against her former employers. August reaches the radio station and transmits the ledger live as sirens converge. Elena is captured covering their escape. POV: August. Beat: climax; truth costs everything it touches.

chapters.title: The Deep Safehouse
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the scandal has toppled careers but not convictions; the machine absorbs the damage. August, officially dead, lives under a new name in a remote safehouse Elena arranged before her arrest. Mara sends him one message: 'Debt cleared.' He sleeps through the night for the first time — as someone else entirely. POV: August. Beat: bittersweet resolution; survival purchased with selfhood.
